_comment: The Intune and endpoint checklist (Lib/Get-TPIntuneChecklist.ps1). Checks follow Maester's tests by id; the rules are the tool's port, with the differences named in the Lib file. Antivirus values are Maester's (some are operational preferences, not security requirements). Recommended is what to set in the Intune admin center; the tool changes nothing.

asrStandardRules.Name: Block credential stealing from the Windows local security authority subsystem (lsass.exe)
Block abuse of exploited vulnerable signed drivers
Block persistence through WMI event subscription

checks.Title: Devices with no compliance policy are marked not compliant
checks.Why: By default Intune marks a device that no compliance policy reaches as Compliant, so a Conditional Access policy requiring a compliant device lets it in.
checks.Recommended: Intune admin center: Devices, Compliance, Compliance settings: "Mark devices with no compliance policy assigned as" = Not compliant.

checks.Title: A device clean-up rule is configured
checks.Why: Devices that stopped checking in stay in the inventory and in compliance reports for ever.
checks.Recommended: Intune admin center: Devices, Device clean-up rules: hide devices that have not checked in for 90 days (or your own period).

checks.Title: The MDM authority is Intune
checks.Why: A tenant whose MDM authority is not Intune cannot manage devices through Intune.
checks.Recommended: Set the MDM authority to Intune (Intune admin center, Tenant administration).

checks.Title: An iOS compliance policy blocks jailbroken devices
checks.Why: A jailbroken iPhone or iPad has iOS security turned off and is still reported compliant.
checks.Recommended: iOS/iPadOS compliance policy, Device Health: Jailbroken devices = Block.

checks.Title: An iOS compliance policy requires a strong passcode
checks.Why: Whoever holds the device reaches corporate mail and the Authenticator app on it.
checks.Recommended: iOS/iPadOS compliance policy, System Security: Require a password; Simple passwords = Block; Minimum password length = 6 or more; Maximum minutes after screen lock = 15 or less.

checks.Title: An iOS compliance policy sets a minimum OS version
checks.Why: A device several versions behind keeps every vulnerability those versions fixed and stays compliant.
checks.Recommended: iOS/iPadOS compliance policy, Device Properties: Minimum OS version = the oldest release you support.

checks.Title: An iOS compliance policy requires a Defender risk level
checks.Why: Ties device access to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint's view of the device.
checks.Recommended: iOS/iPadOS compliance policy, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint: Require the device to be at or under the machine risk score = Clear, Low or Medium (needs the Defender connector).

checks.Title: An Android compliance policy blocks rooted devices
checks.Why: A rooted device has Android security turned off and is still reported compliant.
checks.Recommended: Android Enterprise compliance policy, Device Health: Rooted devices = Block.

checks.Title: An Android compliance policy requires a strong password
checks.Why: Whoever holds the device reaches corporate data on it.
checks.Recommended: Android Enterprise compliance policy, System Security: Require a password; Minimum password length = 6 or more; Maximum minutes of inactivity = 15 or less.

checks.Title: An Android compliance policy requires a recent security patch level
checks.Why: An unpatched Android device keeps known vulnerabilities and stays compliant.
checks.Recommended: Android Enterprise compliance policy, Device Properties: Minimum security patch level = a date within the last year (review it every quarter).

checks.Title: An Android compliance policy requires device threat protection
checks.Why: Lets a mobile threat defense product (such as Defender for Endpoint) mark a compromised device non-compliant.
checks.Recommended: Android Enterprise compliance policy, Device Health: Require the device to be at or under the Device Threat Level = Secured, Low or Medium (needs a threat defense connector).

checks.Title: An Android compliance policy blocks USB debugging
checks.Why: USB debugging lets a computer read and change the device.
checks.Recommended: Android compliance policy, System Security: Block USB debugging on device.

checks.Title: An Android compliance policy blocks devices managed with device administrator
checks.Why: Device administrator management is deprecated by Google and Microsoft and gives Intune little control.
checks.Recommended: Android compliance policy: Block devices managed with device administrator, and move devices to Android Enterprise.

checks.Title: A macOS compliance policy requires System Integrity Protection
checks.Why: With SIP off, malware can change protected system files.
checks.Recommended: macOS compliance policy, Device Health: Require system integrity protection.

checks.Title: A macOS compliance policy restricts app download locations (Gatekeeper)
checks.Why: Gatekeeper off lets an app from anywhere run without a check.
checks.Recommended: macOS compliance policy, System Security: Gatekeeper, allow apps downloaded from = Mac App Store and identified developers (or Mac App Store).

checks.Title: A macOS compliance policy requires a Defender risk level
checks.Why: Ties device access to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint's view of the Mac.
checks.Recommended: macOS compliance policy, Microsoft Defender for Endpoint: Require the device to be at or under the machine risk score.

checks.Title: The standard protection ASR rules are on
checks.Why: Microsoft's three standard protection rules (credential theft from LSASS, vulnerable signed drivers, WMI persistence) block common attack techniques with almost no business impact.
checks.Recommended: Endpoint security, Attack surface reduction rules: set "Block credential stealing from LSASS", "Block abuse of exploited vulnerable signed drivers" and "Block persistence through WMI event subscription" to Block, and assign it to every Windows device.

checks.Title: Windows LAPS backs up to Entra ID with a strong password
checks.Why: The local administrator password should be unique per device, strong, kept in Entra ID and rotated after use.
checks.Recommended: Endpoint security, Account protection, Local admin password solution: Backup Directory = Microsoft Entra ID; Password Complexity = large + small + numbers + special; Password Length = 14 or more; Post-authentication actions = reset the password (and log off or reboot).

checks.Title: Archive scanning is on
checks.Why: Maester checks this value in every assigned Microsoft Defender Antivirus policy.
checks.Recommended: Endpoint security, Antivirus policy: Allow Archive Scanning = Allowed.

checks.Title: Behavior monitoring is on
checks.Why: Maester checks this value in every assigned Microsoft Defender Antivirus policy.
checks.Recommended: Endpoint security, Antivirus policy: Allow Behavior Monitoring = Allowed.

checks.Title: Cloud protection is on
checks.Why: Maester checks this value in every assigned Microsoft Defender Antivirus policy.
checks.Recommended: Endpoint security, Antivirus policy: Allow Cloud Protection = Allowed.

checks.Title: Email scanning is on
checks.Why: Maester checks this value in every assigned Microsoft Defender Antivirus policy.
checks.Recommended: Endpoint security, Antivirus policy: Allow Email Scanning = Allowed.

checks.Title: Script scanning is on
checks.Why: Maester checks this value in every assigned Microsoft Defender Antivirus policy.
checks.Recommended: Endpoint security, Antivirus policy: Allow Script Scanning = Allowed.

checks.Title: Real-time monitoring is on
checks.Why: Maester checks this value in every assigned Microsoft Defender Antivirus policy.
checks.Recommended: Endpoint security, Antivirus policy: Allow Realtime Monitoring = Allowed.

checks.Title: Full scans include removable drives
checks.Why: Maester checks this value in every assigned Microsoft Defender Antivirus policy.
checks.Recommended: Endpoint security, Antivirus policy: Allow Full Scan Removable Drive Scanning = Allowed.

checks.Title: Full scans skip mapped network drives (Maester: performance)
checks.Why: Maester checks this value in every assigned Microsoft Defender Antivirus policy.
checks.Recommended: Endpoint security, Antivirus policy: Allow Full Scan On Mapped Network Drives = Not allowed.

checks.Title: Network files are scanned
checks.Why: Maester checks this value in every assigned Microsoft Defender Antivirus policy.
checks.Recommended: Endpoint security, Antivirus policy: Allow scanning of network files = Allowed.

checks.Title: Average CPU load during a scan is 20 to 30 percent
checks.Why: Maester checks this value in every assigned Microsoft Defender Antivirus policy.
checks.Recommended: Endpoint security, Antivirus policy: Avg CPU Load Factor = 20 to 30.

checks.Title: A scan is scheduled
checks.Why: Maester checks this value in every assigned Microsoft Defender Antivirus policy.
checks.Recommended: Endpoint security, Antivirus policy: Schedule Scan Day = Every day (or a set day).

checks.Title: Signatures are checked before a scan
checks.Why: Maester checks this value in every assigned Microsoft Defender Antivirus policy.
checks.Recommended: Endpoint security, Antivirus policy: Check For Signatures Before Running Scan = Enabled.

checks.Title: Cloud block level is High or higher
checks.Why: Maester checks this value in every assigned Microsoft Defender Antivirus policy.
checks.Recommended: Endpoint security, Antivirus policy: Cloud Block Level = High, High Plus or Zero Tolerance.

checks.Title: Cloud extended timeout is 30 to 50 seconds
checks.Why: Maester checks this value in every assigned Microsoft Defender Antivirus policy.
checks.Recommended: Endpoint security, Antivirus policy: Cloud Extended Timeout = 30 to 50.

checks.Title: Signatures update every 1 to 4 hours
checks.Why: Maester checks this value in every assigned Microsoft Defender Antivirus policy.
checks.Recommended: Endpoint security, Antivirus policy: Signature Update Interval = 1 to 4.

checks.Title: Potentially unwanted app protection is on
checks.Why: Maester checks this value in every assigned Microsoft Defender Antivirus policy.
checks.Recommended: Endpoint security, Antivirus policy: PUA Protection = On (or Audit).

checks.Title: Network protection is on
checks.Why: Maester checks this value in every assigned Microsoft Defender Antivirus policy.
checks.Recommended: Endpoint security, Antivirus policy: Enable Network Protection = Enabled (block mode), or audit.

checks.Title: Local administrators cannot add their own exclusions
checks.Why: Maester checks this value in every assigned Microsoft Defender Antivirus policy.
checks.Recommended: Endpoint security, Antivirus policy: Disable Local Admin Merge = Enabled.

checks.Title: Real-time scanning watches incoming files (all files or incoming)
checks.Why: Maester checks this value in every assigned Microsoft Defender Antivirus policy.
checks.Recommended: Endpoint security, Antivirus policy: Real Time Scan Direction = Monitor all files.

checks.Title: Cleaned malware is kept for at least 30 days
checks.Why: Maester checks this value in every assigned Microsoft Defender Antivirus policy.
checks.Recommended: Endpoint security, Antivirus policy: Days To Retain Cleaned Malware = 30 or more.

checks.Title: Catch-up full scans are off
checks.Why: Maester checks this value in every assigned Microsoft Defender Antivirus policy.
checks.Recommended: Endpoint security, Antivirus policy: Disable Catchup Full Scan = Disabled catch-up (the policy value 1).

checks.Title: Catch-up quick scans are off
checks.Why: Maester checks this value in every assigned Microsoft Defender Antivirus policy.
checks.Recommended: Endpoint security, Antivirus policy: Disable Catchup Quick Scan = Disabled catch-up (the policy value 1).

checks.Title: Safe samples are submitted automatically
checks.Why: Maester checks this value in every assigned Microsoft Defender Antivirus policy. The tool accepts the two values that send samples automatically (1 safe samples, 3 all samples); Maester also accepts 2, which is "never send".
checks.Recommended: Endpoint security, Antivirus policy: Submit Samples Consent = Send safe samples automatically (or send all samples automatically).

checks.Title: An iOS app protection policy requires a strong app PIN
checks.Why: Without a PIN, anyone holding an unlocked phone opens company mail and files in the managed apps.
checks.Recommended: iOS app protection policy, Access requirements: PIN for access = Require; Simple PIN = Block; Select minimum PIN length = 6 or more; PIN reset after number of days and Maximum PIN attempts = 5 or fewer.

checks.Title: An iOS app protection policy keeps organization data inside managed apps
checks.Why: Without it, company data can be copied, saved or backed up to personal apps and cloud storage.
checks.Recommended: iOS app protection policy, Data protection: Send org data to other apps = Policy managed apps; Restrict cut, copy and paste = Policy managed apps (with paste in); Save copies of org data = Block; Backup org data = Block.

checks.Title: An iOS app protection policy encrypts organization data
checks.Why: Encryption keeps company data unreadable when the device is locked or lost.
checks.Recommended: iOS app protection policy, Data protection: Encrypt org data = Require (When device is locked).

checks.Title: An iOS app protection policy requires a minimum OS and app version
checks.Why: An outdated iOS or app version keeps known vulnerabilities and still opens company data.
checks.Recommended: iOS app protection policy, Conditional launch: Min OS version and Min app version, with Block access.

checks.Title: An iOS app protection policy limits offline access to organization data
checks.Why: A device that stops checking in keeps company data for ever unless access is blocked and the data wiped.
checks.Recommended: iOS app protection policy, Conditional launch: Offline grace period = Block access after 12 hours or less; Wipe data after 90 days or less.

checks.Title: An iOS app protection policy acts on the device threat level
checks.Why: Lets a mobile threat defense product (such as Defender for Endpoint) keep a compromised phone out of company data.
checks.Recommended: iOS app protection policy, Conditional launch: Max allowed device threat level = Secured, Low or Medium, action Block access (needs a threat defense connector).

checks.Title: An Android app protection policy requires a strong app PIN
checks.Why: Without a PIN, anyone holding an unlocked phone opens company mail and files in the managed apps.
checks.Recommended: Android app protection policy, Access requirements: PIN for access = Require; Simple PIN = Block; Select minimum PIN length = 6 or more; PIN reset after number of days and Maximum PIN attempts = 5 or fewer.

checks.Title: An Android app protection policy keeps organization data inside managed apps
checks.Why: Without it, company data can be copied, saved or backed up to personal apps and cloud storage.
checks.Recommended: Android app protection policy, Data protection: Send org data to other apps = Policy managed apps; Restrict cut, copy and paste = Policy managed apps (with paste in); Save copies of org data = Block; Backup org data = Block.

checks.Title: An Android app protection policy encrypts organization data
checks.Why: Encryption keeps company data unreadable on a lost device; Android must not waive it because the device is encrypted.
checks.Recommended: Android app protection policy, Data protection: Encrypt org data = Require; Encrypt org data on enrolled devices = Require (do not waive it).

checks.Title: An Android app protection policy requires a minimum OS and app version
checks.Why: An outdated Android or app version keeps known vulnerabilities and still opens company data.
checks.Recommended: Android app protection policy, Conditional launch: Min OS version and Min app version (and Min patch version), with Block access.

checks.Title: An Android app protection policy limits offline access to organization data
checks.Why: A device that stops checking in keeps company data for ever unless access is blocked and the data wiped.
checks.Recommended: Android app protection policy, Conditional launch: Offline grace period = Block access after 12 hours or less; Wipe data after 90 days or less.

checks.Title: An Android app protection policy acts on the device threat level
checks.Why: Lets a mobile threat defense product keep a compromised phone out of company data.
checks.Recommended: Android app protection policy, Conditional launch: Max allowed device threat level = Secured, Low or Medium, action Block access (needs a threat defense connector).

checks.Title: An Android app protection policy blocks screen capture of organization data
checks.Why: Screenshots and screen recording copy company data out of the managed apps.
checks.Recommended: Android app protection policy, Data protection: Screen capture and Google Assistant = Block.

checks.Title: An Android app protection policy requires Play Integrity device attestation
checks.Why: Play Integrity tells a genuine, unmodified Android device from a rooted or emulated one.
checks.Recommended: Android app protection policy, Conditional launch: Play integrity verdict = Basic integrity (and certified devices), action Block access.
